answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pricing influence quadratically: the first identity costs one unit, the second four, the third nine, so weight grows only as the square root of spending. A lone honest agent pays once for a clear signal, while a farm cloning itself must fund an ever-steeper vine of copies. Each extra copy adds little voice but much cost, like ivory carved thinner with every duplicate, until flooding a vote costs more than any gain it could buy.
